entry.content:
Toyota put snow tracks on a Tundra, Tacoma, 4Runner, Land Cruiser and Sequoia, covered all five in white camouflage with gloss black trim, and named the family Snowhunter. Each is set up for a different winter job. The Tundra is the mobile basecamp, and its top rack drops down so gear is easier to load. The Tacoma carries an awning and recovery gear for tight trails, the Land Cruiser a ski rack, and the 4Runner and Sequoia Thule cargo boxes. They are prototypes that Toyota says may not be allowed on public roads, perhaps an acceptable limitation for vehicles built to cross deep snow.

entry.content:
In addition to being emissions-free, electric powertrains allow for exploration of the outdoors without the noise created by ICE-powered transports. For snowy locales, Moonbikes provides a solid option with their electric snowmobile. It has an innovative propulsion system that is both highly efficient and totally silent, with a top speed of 26 mph and the ability to handle powder up to 12 inches deep. The low center gravity and modest weight — under 200 lbs with a single battery — make it extremely easy to ride, while the 28-inch width makes it easy to transport. It can run up to 1.5 hours with a single battery in temperatures as low as -13°F and is assembled in France by Bosch. Ready for adventure wherever you can find snow, it ships in 1-2 weeks with a single battery and standard charger.

entry.content:
Named for Masataka Taketsuru, the father of Japanese whisky, this exceptional 21-year-old expression brings together the distinctive characters of Nikka's Yoichi and Miyagikyo distilleries. Crafted entirely from malt whisky and matured in a combination of ex-bourbon and sherry casks, it offers layers of ripe fruit, dark chocolate, honey, and subtle peat smoke. The palate introduces peach, vanilla, roasted nuts, and warm spices before a long, evolving finish. A multiple-time winner of World's Best Blended Malt Whisky honors, Taketsuru 21 has become increasingly sought after as older Japanese whisky stocks have grown scarce.

entry.summary: Since 1933, Tower Optical has produced the iconic quarter-operated chrome binocular viewers that have framed generations of American sightseeing, from Niagara Falls and the Empire State Building to the Golden Gate Bridge, Gettysburg, and national park overlooks. Now, as the compa
entry.content:
Since 1933, Tower Optical has produced the iconic quarter-operated chrome binocular viewers that have framed generations of American sightseeing, from Niagara Falls and the Empire State Building to the Golden Gate Bridge, Gettysburg, and national park overlooks. Now, as the company's 2,000-machine fleet transitions to tap-to-pay, a handful of coin-era originals are leaving their posts for private ownership in small, numbered batches. Each 300-pound viewer is professionally refurbished at Tower Optical's original Norwalk, Connecticut shop, retaining its 10x optics, chrome-plated bronze housing, cast-iron pedestal, and coin-operated mechanism, or configured for free use. Select examples carry decades of documented history from the landmarks they once overlooked, accompanied by their original handwritten maintenance history card, provenance report, and a lifetime parts warranty. Release № 3 includes viewers retired from the Empire State Building, Niagara Falls, Golden Gate Bridge, and Ellis Island. It's less a souvenir than a piece of American history brought home. Enjoy this limited release ahead of the holiday season.

entry.content:

The Audacious IV, from British builder Audacious Automotive, reinterprets it on a B7 Audi RS4 with a 4.2-liter V8, Torsen all-wheel drive and a six-speed manual. The engine comes in four versions, from 600 supercharged horsepower to V8s that rev to 10,000 rpm. Owners pick hand-formed steel and aluminum bodywork built around an original Quattro's roof and glass, or an all-new carbon fiber body that needs no donor car. The debut car is trimmed in tan leather and tartan, and Audacious claims 0 to 60 mph in under 3.4 seconds. Commissions are open for up to 50 cars.

entry.content:
Lectric takes its popular folding e-bike into its third generation with the XP Lite3, adding thoughtful upgrades while keeping the approachable $799 price point. The 49-pound frame packs a Stealth M24 motor, five pedal-assist modes, speeds up to 20 mph, and up to 80 miles of range. Available in a range of fresh colorways, the XP Lite3 delivers a more refined take on compact, everyday electric transportation.
